energy.title: Power
energy.draftNote: Cut groups stay a draft — they are never written to your hangar.

tooltip.weapons: Cuts power to the whole group. With no power the guns will not fire — sustained DPS drops to 0 and EM falls noticeably. Click again to switch it back on.
tooltip.shields: Gold marks the minimum the active generators need. Below it the shield fails, and the passive backup goes with it.
tooltip.thrusters: Main and manoeuvring thrusters. At zero the ship still steers, but it has no thrust.
tooltip.coolers: The more segments, the lower the cooling load — and the lower your IR signature. Cooling is the price of staying quiet.
tooltip.radar: Sets how far you see. More power means more range — and more EM, so more visibility to everyone else.
tooltip.lifeSupport: Oxygen and pressure. At zero a clock starts running — the game files do not say how long.
tooltip.quantum: Has no channel in SCM. It only draws power in NAV — and there the shield goes dark instead.
tooltip.tractor: Off. It only draws power once you use it.
tooltip.ir: Your heat signature. It rises with the cooling load and with everything that draws power. Low IR means thermal sensors pick you up later.
tooltip.em: The sum of every powered component. Shields and coolers are the biggest items — cut a group and its share disappears. What a part emits comes from the game files; energy weapons carry 0 there.
tooltip.crossSection: How large you look on radar. It comes from the hull, not the equipment — no loadout changes it.
tooltip.coolingLoad: How much of the installed cooling capacity is in use right now. Above 100 % the ship runs hot and the IR signature spikes.

moduleSection.shieldsNote: Every bay in this block is a swappable shield generator, including the ones that ship empty. The shield control module sits with the fixed systems: it is not a shield of its own and cannot be swapped in game.
moduleSection.countermeasuresNote: Launchers cannot be changed in game, so this block is for reference only. Decoys pull heat-seeking missiles away, noise (chaff) blinds radar-guided ones. How many you need depends on the signature values of the round that is fired — this extract does not link a launcher to its round, so no per-launcher signature values are shown.

module.shieldNote: All three are shield generators and all three can be swapped. The passive one costs no power and still counts fully towards the pool — but it hangs off the active ones: if they fail, the backup goes with them.

about.title: About SC Companion
about.subtitle: Who runs this site, what it does, and where the code lives.

what.title: What is this?
what.p1: Star Citizen Companion (SCC) is a free, non-commercial companion app for the space sim Star Citizen: Verse news, a ship and equipment codex, and personal hangar and loadout tools.
what.p2: News, codex and release notes are browsable without an account. An account is only needed for personal features such as your hangar, and registration is currently invite-only.

openSource.title: Open source
openSource.p1: The entire application is developed in the open. Every change is publicly reviewable on GitHub — this is the same code that runs on this site.

data.title: Your data
data.p1: SCC shows no ads and stores only what the features need. Product analytics run through PostHog on EU servers. Details are in the privacy policy:

affiliation.title: Fan project — not affiliated
affiliation.p1: SCC is an unofficial fan project made by the community. It is not affiliated with, endorsed by, or sponsored by Cloud Imperium Games or Roberts Space Industries, and it never asks for your RSI account credentials.

contact.title: Contact
contact.p1: The fastest way to reach the maintainers:

summary.title: In short
summary.signIn: There are exactly two ways to sign in: e-mail address and password, or your Google account. The Google route is optional and does send data to Google.
summary.noTracking: No advertising trackers. Product analytics via PostHog (EU) only run if you allow them — off by default.
summary.minimal: Only the data the features need — nothing is sold or shared for marketing.
summary.euHosting: Application data is stored in the EU (Supabase, region eu-central-1 / Frankfurt).

hosting.title: Hosting and server logs
hosting.p1: This site is delivered by Vercel Inc. (USA). When you visit, Vercel technically processes your IP address and browser information to serve the page and to protect the service (legitimate interest, Art. 6(1)(f) GDPR).
hosting.p2: The app itself is a static web application; there is no server-side page rendering with personal data.

account.title: Account and application data
account.p1: You only need an account for the personal features (hangar, loadouts, settings, feedback). News, codex and release notes work without one. There are exactly two ways to sign in: e-mail address plus password, or the "Continue with Google" button. The app uses no other method — no magic links, no SMS codes, no further social logins — and there is no sign-up form: accounts are created by an invitation an administrator sends to your e-mail address.
account.p2: For sign-in, our backend provider Supabase keeps an auth record about you in the EU region eu-central-1 (Frankfurt): your e-mail address, a salted password hash when you use password sign-in (never the plaintext password), the linked sign-in methods, and timestamps such as invitation, creation and last sign-in.
account.p3: On top of that there is a profile record with what the app needs for you: a display name (initially the part of your e-mail address before the @), the username you pick yourself, your language and game-channel preference, optionally your RSI handle and your flagship, plus your role (viewer, collaborator, admin) and whether your account is approved. Role and approval decide what you may see and do.
account.p4: Feature data you create (hangar ships, loadouts, ship links, saved drafts, settings) is stored under your account and is only readable by you — enforced with row-level security in the database. One obvious exception: feedback you send is visible to the maintainers, with your account as the sender so they can reply.
account.p5: Accounts are invite-only. Sign-ups that are not approved never get past the login page and can be removed together with their data.

google.title: Signing in with Google
google.p1: The Google route is optional — e-mail and password get you in without Google. When you tap "Continue with Google", the app sends you to Google's sign-in page (accounts.google.com). Google thereby learns that you are signing in to SC Companion, along with the technical data every page visit carries (IP address, browser, time). The provider is Google Ireland Limited (Ireland) or Google LLC (USA).
google.p2: After a successful sign-in, Google returns data to us that Supabase stores in your account's auth record: your Google account id, your e-mail address, the name you have on file with Google, and the URL of your Google profile picture. Almost none of it is displayed — your name appears in the account menu, and only for as long as you have not set your own username; the app never loads your profile picture, it only shows the first letter as an initial.
google.p3: Nothing flows back to Google beyond the sign-in itself — no hangar, codex or usage data. What Google does with the sign-in data on its side is governed by Google's own privacy policy:
google.p4: The legal basis for this route is your consent (Art. 6(1)(a) GDPR): you decide anew at every sign-in whether to use it. If you want to get rid of an existing Google link, contact the maintainers via the routes in the site notice.

local.title: Cookies, local storage and your session
local.p1: SCC sets no cookies — neither its own nor any from ad networks. Instead the app uses your browser's local storage, for these entries:

keys.session: sc.auth — your sign-in session: a short-lived access token and a refresh token from Supabase. While you stay signed in, the app renews the access token automatically in the background; signing out deletes the entry. Clearing your browser's site data signs you out as well.
keys.consent: sc.consent — your decision about the storage categories, so we do not ask again on every visit.
keys.composer: sc.composer.sendOnEnter — whether the Enter key sends in the feedback box or adds a new line.
keys.preferences: "Preferences" category — convenience state such as news filters, saved articles and favorited ships. Only written if you allow it; withdrawing your consent deletes those entries immediately.
keys.statistics: "Statistics" category — the state of the anonymous product analytics (PostHog). Only created if you allow it; withdrawing your consent deletes it immediately.

local.p2: During a Google sign-in there is briefly one extra entry in session storage (sc.oauth-redirect-qs) so that you land back on the page you came from. It disappears when the tab closes at the latest.
local.p3: If you explicitly authorize one of our desktop tools (data uploader, Starscape), the browser hands your session's access token to the program running locally on your machine (127.0.0.1) — not to a third party, and never via the address bar.
local.p4: As an installable web app (PWA), a service worker caches static assets on your device for faster loading and offline use — this cache contains no personal data and can be cleared by uninstalling the app or clearing site data.

thirdParty.title: Third-party services
thirdParty.p1: The app talks to a small, fixed set of services (also technically enforced by our Content-Security-Policy):
thirdParty.supabase: Supabase (database, authentication, file storage) — EU region eu-central-1 (Frankfurt); processes your account and application data on our behalf.
thirdParty.vercel: Vercel Inc. (hosting, CDN) — delivery of the static app.
thirdParty.google: Google Sign-In (Google Ireland Limited / Google LLC) — only if you choose to sign in with Google; details in the "Signing in with Google" section.
thirdParty.posthog: PostHog (product analytics and error diagnostics) — EU cloud (eu.i.posthog.com); captures anonymous usage events and errors, and only after you consent.
thirdParty.fonts: Google Fonts — font files are loaded from Google servers; Google may see your IP address.
thirdParty.rsiMedia: Images in the Verse news are partly loaded straight from Roberts Space Industries servers (media.robertsspaceindustries.com, theverse.robertsspaceindustries.com) — RSI sees your IP address while they load.
thirdParty.gameApis: Public Star Citizen data: status.robertsspaceindustries.com and api.star-citizen.wiki (read-only, no account data is sent).

rights.title: Your rights
rights.p1: Under the GDPR you have the right to access, rectification, erasure, restriction of processing, data portability and objection regarding your personal data. You may also lodge a complaint with a data protection supervisory authority.
rights.p2: Your account can be deleted completely: removing the auth record also removes profile, hangar, loadouts, drafts and uploads through the database cascade. Right now the deletion is carried out by an administrator — the delete button in the settings only works for accounts with the admin role. Request it via the contact routes in the site notice; requests are handled promptly.
rights.p3: You can withdraw your consent for preference storage and statistics at any time in the settings; withdrawal deletes the affected local entries immediately and applies going forward — the lawfulness of processing up to that point is unaffected.

operator.title: Operator
operator.p1: Star Citizen Companion (sc-companion.vercel.app) is a non-commercial, open-source community project. It is maintained by the StarOrga organization and its contributors on GitHub.
operator.p2: The project earns no revenue: no ads, no paid features, no sponsoring.
